risk.rationale: QuickHire Ranker scores and ranks job applicants' CVs with an XGBoost model trained on historical hiring outcomes. It automatically rejects candidates below a cut-off and emails them a rejection. This is an AI system for recruitment and selection, including filtering and evaluating candidates, which falls under Annex III point 4(a). No Art. 5 practice is evident. The system doesn't do emotion recognition, biometric categorisation or social scoring. Video interview scoring is only an idea in the notes. The README claims recruiters can override the AI, but the code sets override_allowed = False, so there is no human override. The Art. 6(3) exemption does not apply, because the system profiles natural persons and materially influences the outcome. The notes show no compliance work: there is no audit logging, the threshold was set by eye, and the model is trained on 2015–2020 hiring data with only an accuracy metric. These gaps are relevant to high-risk obligations (Arts. 9–15) but don't change the tier.
triggers: Annex III 4(a): recruitment and selection, filtering and evaluating candidates
Automated rejection of applicants below a threshold with no human override (override_allowed = False)
Profiling of natural persons from CV data, so the Art. 6(3) exemption is unavailable
Model trained on historical hiring outcomes (bias risk), with no audit logging

requirements.title: No prohibited AI practices
requirements.statement: The system does not implement any practice prohibited by Art. 5(1): subliminal or manipulative techniques, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, crime prediction based solely on profiling, untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion inference in the workplace or in education, or biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits.

checks.description: no emotion recognition / social scoring / face scraping code

requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code or documentation showing the system infers emotions (e.g. from video interviews or voice) of employees/candidates/students, scores people on social behaviour, scrapes facial images, or categorises people by biometrics into sensitive traits. A comment or doc stating that such a feature is NOT implemented is evidence of compliance, not a violation. Mark non_compliant only if a prohibited practice is actually implemented or planned for production.

requirements.title: Risk classification documented
requirements.statement: The provider documents the AI Act risk classification of the system with its rationale: the applicable Annex III area/point if high-risk, the Art. 6(3) assessment if an Annex III system is claimed not to be high-risk, or why the system is limited/minimal risk.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a README section, ADR or compliance document that states the risk tier AND gives a reason (e.g. "Annex III point 4(a) recruitment", "chatbot, transparency obligations under Art. 50", "spam filtering, no Annex III use case"). A bare marketing claim ("fully compliant") is not a classification.

requirements.title: Risk management system documented
requirements.statement: A risk management process is documented for the high-risk system: known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights are identified and evaluated, and targeted mitigation measures with residual-risk acceptance are recorded and kept up to date.

checks.description: a risk assessment / risk register document exists

requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a risk register / risk assessment / model risk management document listing concrete risks (e.g. discrimination, automation bias, data drift), their likelihood/impact and mitigations. A single sentence like "risks are low" is not sufficient (partial at most).

requirements.title: Training data documented (datasheet)
requirements.statement: Training, validation and test data sets are documented: origin and collection process, original purpose for personal data, preparation steps (labelling, cleaning, enrichment), assumptions, and the availability/quantity/suitability of the data.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a datasheet / data card / training-data document. Code that loads a CSV is not documentation. Partial if only some of origin, preparation and splits are described.

requirements.title: Bias examination and mitigation of data sets
requirements.statement: The data sets have been examined for possible biases likely to lead to discrimination (including representativeness for the persons and setting the system is used on), and measures to detect, prevent and mitigate the identified biases are documented with results.
requirements.llm_guidance: Requires an actual bias/fairness analysis with results (metrics per group, findings, mitigations). A plan ("bias audit planned"), a TODO, or merely excluding protected attributes from the features does NOT satisfy this requirement on its own (proxies may remain). Judge from documents and evaluation code/reports.

requirements.title: Technical documentation (Annex IV)
requirements.statement: Technical documentation covering the Annex IV elements exists before deployment: general description and intended purpose, versions, how the system interacts with other software, development methods, design specifications and key design choices, system architecture, and validation/testing procedures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if a document (or set of docs) covers most Annex IV(1)-(2) elements. An architecture overview plus a model card without development/validation information is partial.

requirements.title: Model card for the deployed model
requirements.statement: A model card documents the deployed model: intended use and out-of-scope uses, version, training data summary, evaluation results, capabilities and known limitations.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check that a model card exists and covers intended use, limitations and evaluation results.

requirements.title: Instructions for use for deployers
requirements.statement: Instructions for use are provided to deployers and contain at least: provider identity and contact, intended purpose, level of accuracy and its metrics, known limitations and foreseeable misuse risks, human oversight measures, and how to collect and interpret the logs.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if the instructions contain all the listed elements. If a guide exists but misses accuracy metrics, limitations or log interpretation, the status is partial. Sections marked TBD count as missing.

requirements.title: Interpretable outputs for deployers
requirements.statement: The system provides information that lets deployers interpret each output (e.g. main reasons, feature contributions, reason codes or confidence) rather than a bare score.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that returns explanations/reason codes alongside the score and shows them to the human reviewer. A global feature-importance chart in a notebook alone is partial.

requirements.title: Disclosure of interaction with an AI system
requirements.statement: Natural persons interacting directly with the AI system (e.g. a chatbot) are informed, clearly and at the latest at the first interaction, that they are interacting with an AI system.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for user-facing UI strings (React/HTML templates, chat greeting) that tell users they talk to an AI, shown at the start of the conversation. A statement buried in terms of service is not sufficient.
evidence_queries: you are chatting with an AI

requirements.title: Marking of AI-generated content
requirements.statement: Synthetic text, image, audio or video generated by the system is marked as AI-generated in a machine-readable format (and labelled for the recipient where it is published or delivered).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that adds an AI-generated flag/header/metadata or visible label to each generated message. A TODO or ticket reference to add labelling later means non_compliant. A disclosure that the user talks to an AI (Art. 50(1)) is a different obligation and does not mark the content.

requirements.title: Affected persons informed about high-risk AI use
requirements.statement: Natural persons subject to decisions made or assisted by the high-risk AI system (candidates, applicants, workers) are informed that such a system is used on them.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a candidate/applicant notice, privacy notice or e-mail template that tells the person an AI system is used to assess them. Recruiter-facing UI text does not inform the candidate.

requirements.title: Automatic logging of AI decisions
requirements.statement: The system automatically records an event for each decision/output over its lifetime, with timestamp, input reference, output, model version and (where applicable) the human reviewer, enabling traceability and post-market monitoring.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that writes a structured record for every prediction (custom journal/audit classes count). Commented-out logging calls, TODOs or debug prints do not count. Logging only errors is not decision logging.

requirements.title: Logs retained for at least six months
requirements.statement: Automatically generated decision logs are retained for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and of at least six months (>= 180 days).
requirements.llm_guidance: Find the effective retention of the decision/audit logs (config, Terraform log group, lifecycle rules). Compliant only if >= 180 days. If logs exist but retention is shorter or unbounded deletion is configured, non_compliant. If no logs exist at all, non_compliant.

requirements.title: Human can override or disregard the AI output
requirements.statement: Natural persons overseeing the system can decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse an individual output of the system, and the override is recorded.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an implemented mechanism (API endpoint, UI action, workflow state) letting a human change the outcome. A flag set to False, a README promise without code, or an override limited to admins for model config does not count.

requirements.title: Stop / interrupt mechanism
requirements.statement: Operators can interrupt the system (a 'stop' button, kill switch or similar procedure) so that it halts in a safe state, e.g. automated processing is suspended and cases fall back to manual handling.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept any implemented switch (feature flag, admin endpoint, config) that stops automated decisions and routes work to humans. Infrastructure scaling to zero without a documented procedure is partial.

requirements.title: No adverse decision solely on the AI output
requirements.statement: Decisions adverse to natural persons (e.g. rejection, decline) are not taken automatically on the basis of the AI output alone; a competent human reviews and confirms them, mitigating automation bias.
requirements.llm_guidance: Trace the decision flow in code. If any adverse outcome is set without a human step (e.g. score below threshold -> rejected), it is non_compliant; if only a subset of cases gets human review (e.g. above an amount threshold), partial.

requirements.title: Accuracy levels and metrics declared
requirements.statement: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics (e.g. AUC, precision/recall, error rates) are declared in the documentation accompanying the system (instructions for use and/or model card).
requirements.llm_guidance: Metrics must be declared in documentation shipped with the system, with values. A training script that prints accuracy is not a declaration.

requirements.title: Resilience to errors (fallback / fail-safe)
requirements.statement: The system handles errors, faults and model unavailability safely (e.g. timeouts and exceptions lead to a fail-safe outcome such as routing to manual handling, never to an automatic adverse decision).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for explicit error handling around model inference with a safe fallback. Generic web framework error pages are not sufficient.

requirements.title: Input validation against malformed or adversarial inputs
requirements.statement: Inputs to the model are validated (schema, types, ranges, size limits, file types) before inference to resist malformed or adversarial inputs.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for schema validation (pydantic/zod/marshmallow), constraints and upload limits on the inference path. Reading raw request bodies directly into the model is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Protection of model endpoints against unauthorised use
requirements.statement: Inference and model-management endpoints are protected against unauthorised third parties (authentication and authorisation), so that the system's use, outputs or performance cannot be altered by exploiting vulnerabilities.
requirements.llm_guidance: Every inference and admin route must require authentication; admin/model routes need authorisation. Partial if some sensitive routes are unauthenticated.

requirements.title: Quality management and post-market monitoring procedures
requirements.statement: Documented procedures cover change management of the model/system, validation before release, post-market monitoring of performance in production (e.g. drift), and serious-incident reporting.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if the repository documents change management, pre-release validation, production monitoring AND incident reporting; partial if only some are covered.

requirements.title: Testing against predefined metrics before release
requirements.statement: The system is tested before release against prior defined metrics and thresholds appropriate to its intended purpose (e.g. an automated quality gate failing the build below a minimum AUC).
requirements.llm_guidance: Smoke tests that only check an HTTP 200 are not model validation; require assertions against metric thresholds on held-out data.

requirements.title: Lawful basis documented for each processing purpose
requirements.statement: Each purpose for which personal data is processed has a documented lawful basis under Art. 6(1) (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task or legitimate interests), and consent is collected and recorded where it is the basis relied on.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a privacy notice, record of processing or DPIA naming the lawful basis per purpose. A README claim "fully GDPR compliant" is not evidence of a lawful basis.

requirements.title: Privacy notice provided to data subjects
requirements.statement: Data subjects receive a privacy notice at collection stating the controller and contact details, purposes and lawful basis, recipients, retention period, and their rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection, complaint).
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if a notice covering controller, purposes, legal basis, retention and rights exists and is shown/linked to data subjects. Partial if key items (e.g. retention or rights) are missing.
evidence_queries: how long we keep your data

requirements.title: Storage limitation enforced
requirements.statement: Personal data is kept no longer than necessary for its purpose: a retention period proportionate to the purpose is defined for each data category and enforced automatically (TTL, purge job, lifecycle rule).
requirements.llm_guidance: Check both that a retention period is defined AND enforced in code/IaC, and that it is proportionate (e.g. keeping raw support chats for years without justification is excessive; keeping data "forever" is non_compliant). Defined and enforced but disproportionate -> partial.

requirements.title: Right to erasure implemented
requirements.statement: A mechanism exists to erase a data subject's personal data on request without undue delay (endpoint, admin job or documented procedure covering all stores, including derived data).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an implemented deletion path for a single data subject. Automatic expiry of all data after N days is not an on-request erasure mechanism (partial at most).

requirements.title: Safeguards for solely automated decisions
requirements.statement: Decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects are not based solely on automated processing, or, where an Art. 22(2) exception applies, the data subject can obtain human intervention, express their point of view and contest the decision.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if no significant decision is fully automated, OR if automated decisions come with an implemented contest/appeal path leading to human review. Non_compliant if decisions are fully automated with no recourse.

requirements.title: Meaningful information about the logic involved
requirements.statement: Data subjects are informed of the existence of automated decision-making/profiling and receive meaningful information about the logic involved and its envisaged consequences.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an applicant/candidate-facing explanation of the main factors used and the consequences. Internal model documentation does not inform data subjects.

requirements.title: Data minimisation and privacy by design
requirements.statement: Only personal data necessary for the purpose is collected and used (no unnecessary sensitive or protected attributes as model features), and privacy-by-design measures such as pseudonymisation or redaction are applied before processing or sharing with third parties.
requirements.llm_guidance: Inspect model features and data flows. Using gender/age/nationality as features, or sending raw personal data to a third-party LLM without redaction, is non_compliant. Look for explicit redaction/pseudonymisation code.

requirements.title: Encryption of personal data at rest and in transit
requirements.statement: Personal data is encrypted at rest (databases, object storage, volumes, backups) and in transit (TLS) as appropriate to the risk.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both at-rest and in-transit encryption must be evidenced for all stores holding personal data. Only one of the two -> partial. Self-signed dev certificates in docker-compose do not count for production.

requirements.title: Access control to personal data
requirements.statement: Access to personal data and to administrative functions is restricted to authenticated and authorised personnel (authentication, role-based authorisation, least privilege).
requirements.llm_guidance: Check that endpoints exposing personal data require authentication and that admin/export routes check roles. Unauthenticated upload/listing endpoints are non_compliant.

requirements.title: Record of processing activities
requirements.statement: A record of processing activities is maintained for the system listing purposes, categories of data subjects and personal data, recipients, transfers, retention limits and security measures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a ROPA entry in the repo (markdown/yaml). A DPIA or privacy notice alone is not a ROPA but may be partial if it contains the Art. 30(1) items.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.statement: A DPIA has been carried out for the processing (systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing) and contains a description of the processing, necessity and proportionality assessment, risk assessment and mitigation measures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if a DPIA document with the Art. 35(7) elements exists.

requirements.title: AI use disclosed in user interfaces
requirements.statement: Every interface where a person interacts with the AI system or sees an AI-produced score, ranking, classification or text visibly discloses AI involvement; decision-support UIs state that the output is an AI recommendation and who decides.
requirements.llm_guidance: Inspect UI components, e-mail templates and notification texts. Neutral names like "Smart Score" do not disclose AI involvement.

requirements.title: AI-generated content labelled
requirements.statement: AI-generated text/media delivered to customers carries a visible "AI-generated" label and, where feasible, a machine-readable marker.
requirements.llm_guidance: A banner saying the user chats with an AI is POL-1, not POL-2. Look for per-message labelling or metadata. TODO comments do not count.

requirements.title: Prediction logging with 180-day retention
requirements.statement: Every production prediction/response is logged with timestamp, correlation id, model version, input reference and output, in tamper-resistant storage retained for at least 180 days.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both parts are needed: structured per-prediction logging AND >= 180 days retention. Logging with shorter retention -> partial. No logging -> non_compliant.
evidence_queries: prediction log model version request id

requirements.title: Raw personal-data inputs deleted within 30 days
requirements.statement: Raw inputs containing personal data (documents, messages, transcripts, payloads) are automatically deleted or anonymised within 30 days, unless a documented legal retention obligation applies.
requirements.llm_guidance: Find the retention of each raw-input store. Any raw store kept > 30 days without a documented legal obligation is non_compliant; no automated deletion at all is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Encryption at rest and TLS in transit
requirements.statement: Storage of personal data, model artefacts and logs is encrypted at rest, and all service traffic uses TLS 1.2+.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both at rest and in transit must be shown; one of the two -> partial.

requirements.title: Access control on model endpoints
requirements.statement: Inference and model-management endpoints require authentication (or are declared public and rate-limited), and administrative endpoints enforce role-based authorisation.
requirements.llm_guidance: Enumerate routes. Any undeclared unauthenticated inference/upload route, or an admin route without a role check, is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Human approval of adverse decisions
requirements.statement: Adverse decisions about natural persons (rejection, decline, closure) are approved by a human reviewer who sees the AI output and reasons and can change the outcome, and the approval is logged.
requirements.llm_guidance: Trace adverse outcomes in code. Human approval for only part of the cases (e.g. above an amount threshold) is partial. Automatic rejection is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Model card for every deployed model
requirements.statement: Each deployed model (including third-party models) has a model card covering intended and out-of-scope use, version, training data summary, evaluation metrics, limitations and owner.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check presence and completeness of the model card(s) against the listed fields.

requirements.title: Rate limiting on AI endpoints
requirements.statement: AI endpoints reachable from untrusted networks enforce per-client rate limiting configured in code or configuration.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for rate-limit middleware (express-rate-limit, slowapi), gateway throttling or ingress annotations. Public endpoints without it are non_compliant.

requirements.title: AI incident response procedure
requirements.statement: The repository contains an AI incident response procedure (detection, escalation, reporting) that requires reporting serious incidents to the AI Governance Board within 24 hours.
requirements.llm_guidance: A generic ops runbook without AI incidents or without the 24h governance reporting is partial.

requirements.title: Bias and fairness evaluation before release
requirements.statement: A documented bias and fairness evaluation (metrics and results per protected group, mitigations) exists for the released model and is referenced from the model card.
requirements.llm_guidance: Requires actual results. "Planned", TODOs or excluding protected features only is non_compliant.

verdicts.rationale: The implemented system (E1-E4, E6) is a CV-based ranking and auto-rejection tool. It uses an XGBoost model trained on historical hiring outcomes. It has no code for emotion recognition, social scoring, facial scraping or biometric categorisation. So no Art. 5(1) practice is actually implemented in the code shown. However, E5 lists "add video interview scoring" as a future idea. That could become emotion inference on candidates, which is prohibited in the workplace/employment context. It is only an idea and not a committed production plan, so it does not make the system non_compliant. The evidence also contains no explicit statement that prohibited practices are excluded, and only a limited part of the repository is shown. It is therefore not clearly compliant.
gaps: No explicit statement or policy that Art. 5 prohibited practices are excluded
Planned 'video interview scoring' (E5) is not assessed and could amount to emotion inference
Full repository (e.g. app/model.py FEATURES, app/parser.py) not shown, so features cannot be checked for proxies of sensitive traits
No prohibited-practice screening in the development process
verdicts.remediation: Add a docs/ai-act-art5.md statement that the system does not do emotion inference, social scoring, biometric categorisation or facial scraping. Record that the 'video interview scoring' idea in docs/notes.md must not infer emotions from voice or face. Add an Art. 5 review gate before any such feature ships. Document the FEATURES list to show that no sensitive or biometric traits, or proxies for them, are used. Consider a CI check that flags emotion, face or biometric libraries.

verdicts.rationale: The README (E3) describes a CV-ranking tool that automatically rejects candidates. This is a recruitment/candidate-filtering use case that falls under Annex III point 4(a). It contains no risk-tier statement and no rationale. The only compliance claim is the marketing line "Fully GDPR compliant", which the guidance says is not a classification. The code (E1, E2, E4) shows automated scoring and rejection with no classification documentation. No ADR or compliance document appears in the evidence.
gaps: No stated AI Act risk tier
No reference to Annex III point 4(a) (employment/recruitment) or its rationale
No Art. 6(3) assessment, and one would be unlikely to hold because the system profiles and auto-rejects candidates
No ADR or compliance document
The README makes only an unsupported marketing claim ('Fully GDPR compliant')
verdicts.remediation: Add a docs/risk-classification.md, or a README section, that classifies QuickHire Ranker as high-risk under Annex III point 4(a) (recruitment and selection, CV filtering and evaluation of candidates). Include the rationale: the system scores applicants and automatically rejects them. State that the Art. 6(3) derogation does not apply because the system profiles natural persons and materially influences decisions. Then link the high-risk obligations (Arts. 9-15, human oversight, logging, registration under Art. 49) to follow-up work. Remove the unsupported 'Fully GDPR compliant' claim, and fix the inconsistency between the README's 'recruiters can always override' and `override_allowed = False` in app/main.py.

verdicts.rationale: The only evidence, E1, is a CV parsing code file (app/parser.py). It extracts email, raw text, and crude features such as years of experience, skill count and degree level. It contains no risk register, risk assessment or risk management documentation. There are no identified risks to health, safety or fundamental rights, no likelihood or impact estimates, no mitigations, no residual-risk acceptance and no review process. The code suggests a recruitment-style system with heuristic features that could carry bias risks, but none of this is documented.
gaps: No risk register or risk assessment document
No identification of foreseeable risks (discrimination, bias from crude heuristics, automation bias, PII exposure, parsing errors)
No likelihood/impact evaluation
No documented mitigation measures
No residual-risk acceptance record
No evidence of iterative review or post-market monitoring input
No consideration of reasonably foreseeable misuse
verdicts.remediation: Add a risk management document (e.g. docs/risk_management.md or a risk_register.csv). For each risk, record the description, affected rights, likelihood and impact, mitigation, owner, residual risk and acceptance sign-off. Cover discrimination and proxy bias from features like degree_level and years_experience, brittle regex parsing errors (such as the year-counting heuristic and the "unknown" email fallback), automation bias, PII handling of raw_text and email, and data drift. Add a review cadence and version history, link the register to post-market monitoring, and refer to it from the README and the technical documentation.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence has no datasheet, data card or training-data document. E1 only loads "data/hires_2015_2020.csv" and does a random 80/20 split. Guidance says code that loads a CSV is not documentation. E3 says only that the model is trained on "historical hiring outcomes". It gives no origin, collection process, original purpose of the personal data, preparation steps, assumptions, or the quantity and suitability of the data. E5 and E6 show CVs being kept forever "for retraining", which makes the undocumented provenance and purpose of the personal data a bigger concern. No bias examination or data-gap assessment appears either.
gaps: No datasheet or data card for the training data
Origin and collection process of hires_2015_2020.csv not described
Original purpose of the personal data collection not stated
Labelling, cleaning and enrichment steps not documented
Assumptions about what the data represent not stated (hired=1 as a proxy for suitability)
Size, availability and suitability of the data not assessed
Train/validation/test split is not documented (only an unseeded 80/20 split, no validation set)
No bias examination or data-gap analysis
The data file is not in the repository and has no provenance record
verdicts.remediation: Add docs/datasheet.md (or a data card) for the training data, following the Datasheets for Datasets template. It should cover: (1) the origin of data/hires_2015_2020.csv, how it was collected, and the original purpose and legal basis for the personal data; (2) preparation steps such as labelling, cleaning, feature extraction and enrichment; (3) assumptions, including the limits of using past hiring decisions as the label; (4) record counts, time span, class balance and a suitability and representativeness assessment; (5) the train/validation/test split method, with a fixed seed and a separate validation set; (6) a bias examination across protected groups, mitigation measures and known data gaps. Link the datasheet from README.md and from training/train.py. Also state the retention basis for CVs reused for retraining.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence shows no bias or fairness examination of the data sets. The model trains on historical hiring outcomes from 2015–2020 (E2, E5), which can carry past discrimination. Its features include protected attributes and likely proxies: age, gender, nationality_code, zip_code and gap_months (E1). The only evaluation is overall accuracy (E2), with no per-group metrics, representativeness analysis, findings or mitigations. The README claims "Fully GDPR compliant" (E5), but nothing supports it. Automatic rejection runs at a fixed threshold with no fairness checks (E4, E7).
gaps: No bias or fairness analysis of the training data
No per-group metrics (selection rate, disparate impact, equalized odds) by gender, age or nationality
No representativeness assessment of data/hires_2015_2020.csv for the applicant population
Protected attributes and proxies (age, gender, nationality_code, zip_code, gap_months) used as model features without justification
No documented mitigation measures, such as reweighting, feature removal or threshold calibration
No data governance documentation covering origin, assumptions, gaps or feedback-loop risk from retraining on stored CVs
Evaluation limited to overall accuracy, with an unstratified random split
verdicts.remediation: 1) Add a bias audit (e.g. training/bias_audit.py using fairlearn or aif360). It should compute selection rate, TPR/FPR and disparate-impact ratio per group (gender, age band, nationality, zip/region) on the data and on model outputs. Also test proxy correlation (zip_code, gap_months, nationality_code). 2) Commit the results as docs/data_governance/bias_report.md, with findings and thresholds. 3) Document the dataset's origin, collection purpose, representativeness versus current applicants, labelling assumptions (hired=1 as a proxy for merit) and data gaps. 4) Implement and document mitigations: remove or justify protected attributes and proxies, reweight or resample, calibrate per-group thresholds, and run fairness gates in CI before model release. 5) Account for feedback loops from retraining on stored CVs, and monitor fairness after deployment. 6) Remove the unsupported 'Fully GDPR compliant' claim from the README until this is done.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence has no Annex IV technical documentation. The README (E4) is a marketing-style quick start with a one-line model note. It has no intended purpose statement, version information, development methodology, design rationale, architecture description, or validation procedures. It also makes unsupported claims, such as "Fully GDPR compliant" and "Recruiters can always override the AI". E1 contradicts the override claim, because `override_allowed = False`. The training script (E3) only prints a single accuracy figure on a random split. It has no documented validation procedure and no data provenance. The Dockerfile (E5) and code (E1, E2, E6) show deployment and features, but they are not documentation. E6 uses sensitive and proxy features (age, gender, nationality, zip code), and nothing documents the design choices or trade-offs behind them.
gaps: No technical documentation file (e.g. docs/technical_documentation.md)
Intended purpose, provider name and system versioning not documented
Interaction with other software (email, parser) and forms of placing on market not described
Development methods and use of third-party or pre-trained tools not described
Design specifications, key design choices, assumptions and trade-offs not documented, including use of age, gender and nationality features
System architecture and computational resources not described
Training data datasheet missing (hires_2015_2020.csv provenance, scope, bias)
Validation and testing procedures missing beyond a single accuracy print
Instructions for use and user interface description for deployers missing
Risk management, human oversight and logging measures not documented
verdicts.remediation: Create docs/technical_documentation.md, or a docs/annex_iv/ folder, that follows Annex IV. Cover these points. (1) General description: intended purpose (CV ranking and auto-rejection), provider, version history, the software dependencies with their versions, the Docker/API delivery form, hardware requirements, and instructions for use. (2) Development: training pipeline steps, XGBoost and third-party libraries, a datasheet for hires_2015_2020.csv (provenance, labelling, bias analysis), and the rationale for each feature. Justify or remove age, gender, nationality_code and zip_code. (3) Architecture: a diagram of the Flask app, parser, model and emailer, plus the compute used for training. (4) Validation: a test plan, held-out and per-group fairness metrics, accuracy and error rates, and test logs. (5) Monitoring, human oversight and logging. Correct the README's misleading claims about GDPR compliance and recruiter override. Keep the documentation under version control and update it with each release.

verdicts.rationale: No model card file appears in the evidence. The README "Model" section (E5) has only two sentences: the model is trained by training/train.py on historical hiring outcomes, and you can retrain whenever you like. It gives no intended or out-of-scope use, version, training data summary, evaluation results or limitations. The training script (E4) prints a single overall accuracy and stores no results. It uses data/hires_2015_2020.csv. The model uses protected or proxy features such as age, gender, nationality_code and zip_code (E7). These are exactly the risks and limitations a model card should disclose.
gaps: No MODEL_CARD file
Intended use and out-of-scope uses not documented
Model version not documented (only the file name qh-xgb.pkl)
No training data summary (data/hires_2015_2020.csv, its provenance, period or demographics)
No evaluation results beyond a printed overall accuracy; nothing for specific groups
Known limitations and bias risks not documented, including use of age, gender, nationality and zip code
Human oversight and automated rejection limits not described
verdicts.remediation: Add MODEL_CARD.md at the repository root and keep it current with each retrain. Cover: model name and version (tie to the qh-xgb.pkl artifact); intended use (CV ranking with human review) and out-of-scope uses (e.g. fully automated rejection); training data (source, 2015-2020 period, size, label definition, demographic composition); features used, with justification for or removal of age, gender, nationality_code and zip_code; evaluation (accuracy, precision/recall, AUC, and per-group fairness metrics such as selection-rate ratios); known limitations, historical bias risks and foreseeable unintended outcomes; and human oversight measures. Make training/train.py write its evaluation metrics to a versioned file that the card references. Link the card from the README.

verdicts.rationale: No dedicated instructions-for-use document for deployers exists in the evidence. The README (E2) is a marketing and quick-start document. It gives a loose purpose (ranking and auto-rejecting CVs) but has no provider identity or contact, no accuracy metrics, and no limitations or misuse risks. The accuracy computation in training/train.py (E6) only prints to stdout and is not documented for deployers. E2 claims that recruiters can always override the AI, but E4 shows override_allowed = False, so the human oversight information is incorrect. The code has no audit logging (E4/E5, "TODO: add audit logging"), so there is nothing to explain about collecting or interpreting logs. docs/notes.md (E7) is an internal dev note that defers compliance.
gaps: No instructions-for-use document for deployers
Provider identity and contact details missing
Accuracy level and metrics not documented (only printed in train.py)
Robustness and cybersecurity levels not documented
Known limitations and foreseeable misuse risks missing (for example bias, and the 0.4 threshold rejecting ~55% of applicants)
Human oversight measures missing, and the README claim of recruiter override contradicts the code (override_allowed=False)
No log collection or interpretation guidance; audit logging not implemented
Input and training data specifications missing
verdicts.remediation: Add docs/instructions_for_use.md (or a similar deployer guide) covering: provider name, contact and authorised representative; intended purpose and out-of-scope uses; measured accuracy, with metrics such as precision, recall and per-group performance on a held-out set, plus robustness and cybersecurity results; limitations, bias risks and foreseeable misuse, including the effect of the 0.4 auto-reject threshold; and input data and training data specifications. Document human oversight: implement a real recruiter override, remove the false README claims, and disable fully automated rejection. Implement audit logging of predictions and decisions, without leaking PII, and document where the logs are stored, their format, and how to interpret them. Have the training script save its metrics to a versioned report that the guide references.

verdicts.rationale: The API returns only a bare score and status (E3). The ranking endpoint returns the candidate records sorted by score, with no explanations or reason codes (E3). The frontend shows only email, a rounded "Smart Score" and status (E5). No SHAP/LIME, feature contributions or reason codes appear anywhere, and the training script only prints global accuracy (E6). The README also calls the score an opaque "Smart Score" (E1). Deployers therefore cannot interpret individual outputs, and candidates are auto-rejected on a bare score with no way to override (E2).
gaps: No per-output explanations, reason codes or feature contributions returned by the API
UI shows only a score and status, with no reasons or confidence information
No instructions for use describing explainability capabilities, accuracy or limitations
No documentation of the threshold rationale beyond an eyeballed histogram (E8)
Recruiters cannot override outcomes (override_allowed=False), which limits oversight
verdicts.remediation: Add per-candidate explanations to the /upload_cv and /ranking responses. For example, compute SHAP values with shap.TreeExplainer for the XGBoost model and return the top-N feature contributions or reason codes plus a confidence indicator. Show them in frontend/src/App.tsx, for example in an expandable row. Add deployer documentation (instructions for use) covering the model's accuracy, limitations and how to read the explanations. Stop auto-rejecting on the score alone: route low scores to human review and enable recruiter override. Add tests that check the explanation fields are present.

verdicts.rationale: Applies to limited risk systems; this system is classified as high.
Applies to limited risk systems; this system is classified as high.

Nothing in the evidence tells candidates that an AI system is used to assess them. The only candidate-facing text is the rejection email template (E4). It is generic ("after careful consideration we have decided...") and never mentions AI or automated scoring. The README (E1) and the recruiter UI (E2) talk about the AI, but they are aimed at recruiters and do not inform candidates. The upload flow (E5, E7) shows no notice at CV submission. It scores and auto-rejects applicants without telling them. The dev notes (E3) say compliance is postponed.
gaps: No candidate/applicant notice that an AI system scores and ranks them
Rejection email does not disclose automated/AI decision-making
No privacy notice or consent text at CV upload
No information for workers or their representatives (Art. 26(7))
No documented process for deployers (customers) to inform affected persons
verdicts.remediation: Add a candidate-facing AI-use notice, shown at CV upload (e.g. on the upload page or in the /upload_cv response flow) and linked in a privacy notice. It should say that an AI model (the "Smart Score") is used to assess and rank applications, what role it plays in the decision, and how to contact the employer and request human review. Update TEMPLATE in app/emailer.py to disclose the automated assessment and give a route for human review or contesting the decision. Add an acknowledgment or logging step so the notice is recorded. Give deployer customers a template notice for candidates and for workers' representatives, as Art. 26(7) and 26(11) require. Correct the README claims ("Fully GDPR compliant") that the evidence doesn't support.

verdicts.rationale: The only logging call in the prediction path is commented out, and a TODO says "add audit logging before go-live" (E1, E2). Nothing in the evidence writes a structured record for each decision. The score and status are held only in the in-memory CANDIDATES dict. Auto-rejections are not recorded either. The dev notes say compliance is deferred (E3). Model version, input reference and human reviewer are never recorded, and E2 shows that recruiters cannot override outcomes.
gaps: No active logging of predictions (the logger call is commented out)
No timestamp, input reference, output or model version recorded per decision
Auto-reject decisions are not logged
No human reviewer field, and no override mechanism (override_allowed=False)
Decisions are stored only in an in-memory dict and lost on restart
No log retention or monitoring for post-market surveillance
verdicts.remediation: In app/main.py, add an audit logger or journal class. Call it in upload_cv for every prediction and in auto_reject. Write an append-only structured (JSON) record to durable storage. Each record should hold a UTC timestamp, decision ID, input reference (job_id and a CV file hash or ID, not raw PII), score, threshold, status, model version (for example the hash of models/qh-xgb.pkl), and reviewer ID (null for automatic decisions). Log human overrides when they are added. Set a retention policy and a log-access policy. Replace the in-memory CANDIDATES dict with persistent storage. Remove the commented-out logger line and the TODO.

verdicts.rationale: No decision or audit logs are generated, so nothing is retained for six months or longer. In E1/E2 the only logging call is commented out, and a TODO says "add audit logging before go-live". No log group, retention setting or lifecycle rule appears in the Dockerfile (E3), the notes (E4) or the README (E6). E4 says compliance is deferred. The deterministic pattern for retention_days >= 180 has no match.
gaps: No automatic decision/audit logging active (logger call commented out)
No log retention configuration (>=180 days)
No log storage, log group or lifecycle rule defined
Scores and auto-reject outcomes are only held in in-memory CANDIDATES, which is lost on restart
verdicts.remediation: Enable structured audit logging in app/main.py for every scoring and auto-reject decision. Log the job_id, a pseudonymised candidate ID, score, threshold, model version, outcome and timestamp, and avoid raw PII. Ship the logs to durable storage such as a CloudWatch log group, a Loki volume or an S3 bucket. Set retention of at least 180 days, for example retention_in_days = 365 in Terraform or a lifecycle rule. Make the logs tamper-resistant, and document the retention period in docs and config/settings.yaml. Check that the retention period is consistent with GDPR data minimisation.

verdicts.rationale: No override mechanism is implemented. E4 sets `override_allowed = False` with a comment that recruiters cannot change AI outcomes. E5 shows that candidates scoring below the threshold are auto-rejected and emailed immediately, with no human review state. The only endpoints are `/upload_cv` and `/ranking`, and neither lets a human change an outcome. The README claim in E1 that recruiters can always override the AI is contradicted by the code. No override action is recorded either: E4 has audit logging commented out with a TODO. E2 and E3 add nothing that supports compliance.
gaps: No endpoint or UI action to override, reverse or disregard an AI rejection or score
No human-review workflow state before auto-rejection; the rejection email is sent immediately
No recording of overrides (audit log is commented out)
No stop/interrupt mechanism for the system
README claim of recruiter override is contradicted by the code
No interpretation aids or automation-bias safeguards for overseers
verdicts.remediation: Remove automatic rejection. Set low-scoring candidates to a 'pending_human_review' status and send no email until a recruiter confirms. Add an authenticated endpoint such as POST /candidates/<id>/decision. It should accept accept, reject or override, plus a mandatory reason, and it should record the reviewer ID, timestamp, original score and new outcome in a persistent audit log. Delete the `override_allowed = False` flag. Add a kill switch or pause control for the pipeline. Show reviewers the score and its main contributing factors, and add guidance on automation bias. Correct the README to match the implemented behavior.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence shows no stop, kill switch, or pause mechanism. In E1 and E4, every upload is scored automatically and candidates below the threshold are auto-rejected, with emails sent (`auto_reject`). No flag or endpoint suspends this processing or routes cases to manual handling. The only related flag, `override_allowed = False` (E1), disables recruiter overrides. The README's claim that recruiters can always override (E2) contradicts the code. The Dockerfile (E5) has no operational stop procedure, and no documented procedure appears in the evidence. The deterministic pattern check found nothing.
gaps: No kill switch, feature flag, or admin endpoint to suspend automated scoring or rejection
No fallback to manual review when automation is halted
Recruiter override is disabled (override_allowed = False)
No documented stop or interruption procedure
No audit logging of interventions
verdicts.remediation: Add an operator-controlled switch, such as an env var, config setting, or authenticated admin endpoint like POST /admin/automation/disable. Check it in upload_cv before scoring and auto_reject. When it is set, skip auto-rejection and rejection emails and set candidates to a 'pending_manual_review' status for recruiters. Enable recruiter override of AI outcomes. Add audit logging of switch changes and decisions. Document the stop procedure in a runbook or the README.

verdicts.rationale: The decision flow in E4 sets status to "rejected" and sends a rejection email whenever score < THRESHOLD, with no human step (E3 defines auto_reject, E5 sends the email). E3 sets override_allowed = False and states recruiters cannot change AI outcomes, so the README claim that recruiters can always override (E2) is contradicted by the code. E2 advertises "automatically rejects" and E1 confirms about 55% of applicants are rejected by the 0.4 threshold. The deterministic pattern auto[_-]?reject also matches, so the "absent" check fails.
gaps: Adverse rejections are applied and emailed automatically with no human review
Override is disabled (override_allowed = False)
No review queue or confirmation step before rejection
No audit logging of decisions (commented out, TODO)
No training or guidance on automation bias for reviewers
README claims about override are inaccurate
verdicts.remediation: Remove auto_reject and the threshold-triggered rejection in app/main.py. Have low scores only set status "pending_review" or "flagged", and send no email at that point. Add a recruiter review endpoint (for example POST /candidates/<id>/decision) that requires an authenticated, trained reviewer to confirm or override and records their identity, timestamp and rationale. Send rejection emails only after human confirmation. Enable override (remove the override_allowed=False flag), and log all AI scores and human decisions to an audit trail. Show reviewers the score's limitations and a notice about automation bias. Correct the README claims ("automatically rejects", "Fully GDPR compliant"). Document the oversight procedure and assign competent reviewers.

verdicts.rationale: The only accuracy-related evidence is training/train.py (E1), which prints accuracy_score to stdout. The guidance says that is not a declaration. No model card, instructions for use or other documentation with metric values was provided. E2 is an API status test and has no bearing on accuracy. The deterministic pattern also finds no documented metric values.
gaps: No model card or instructions for use declaring accuracy levels
No documented metric values (accuracy, AUC, precision/recall, error rates)
Only accuracy is computed, and the value is printed and not stored
No per-group or subgroup metrics, which matter for a hiring system
No description of the test dataset or evaluation methodology
Train/test split has no fixed seed, so results are not reproducible
verdicts.remediation: Add a MODEL_CARD.md and/or an instructions-for-use document shipped with the system. It should declare the metrics with values (accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, F1, error rates), the evaluation dataset and the split. Include per-subgroup results and known limitations. Update training/train.py to set a random_state, compute these metrics and write them to a versioned artifact such as metrics.json. Generate the documentation from that artifact so the declared values match the shipped model.

verdicts.rationale: The inference path in app/main.py (E3, E5) has no try/except, timeout, or fallback around parse_cv, extract_features or model.predict_proba. An exception would produce a generic Flask 500 error, which the guidance says is not sufficient. When the score is below the threshold, the code auto-rejects the candidate and sends a rejection email, with no route to manual handling (E5). The model is loaded at import time with no handling for a missing or corrupt file (E3, E7). The only test checks the happy path (E2). No fallback or fail-safe terms appear anywhere in the evidence.
gaps: No error handling or timeout around model inference or CV parsing
No fail-safe route to manual review when the model fails or is unavailable
Automatic rejection with no human fallback
No handling for model load failure at startup
No tests for error or failure scenarios
No health check or degraded-mode behavior
verdicts.remediation: In app/main.py, wrap parse_cv, extract_features and predict_proba in try/except with a timeout. On any failure, set the status to "manual_review" and return a safe response. Never call auto_reject on error, and ideally route all adverse outcomes through human review. Handle model-load failure explicitly at startup, with a health check and a degraded mode that sends everything to manual review. Log errors in an audit log. Add tests that simulate model exceptions, timeouts and a missing model file, and assert that no rejection is made and no email is sent. Document the fallback behavior in the README.

verdicts.rationale: The inference path in app/main.py (E6, E7) reads request.files["cv"] and request.form["job_id"] directly. It does no schema validation, type or range checks, file-type or size limits (no MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH), and no content checks. The raw bytes go to parse_cv and then to model.predict_proba. The user-controlled f.filename and job_id are used unsanitized in file paths, which allows path traversal. The /ranking/<job_id> route also takes an unvalidated parameter (E7). The Dockerfile installs no validation libraries such as pydantic (E8). The deterministic pattern found no validation constructs in the evidence.
gaps: No schema or type validation of job_id and the upload form fields
No file size limit (MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH) on uploads
No file type or MIME or magic-byte check for CVs (PDF only)
Filename and job_id unsanitized, so path traversal is possible
No handling of malformed CVs before parsing and inference
No range or sanity checks on extracted features before predict_proba
No rate limiting or adversarial input detection
verdicts.remediation: Add input validation to app/main.py. Set app.config["MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH"]. Validate job_id with a pydantic model or regex, for example ^[0-9]{1,10}$. Use werkzeug secure_filename, or generate server-side filenames. Allow only PDF, checking the extension, MIME type and magic bytes. Wrap parse_cv in error handling with page and size limits. Validate and clamp the extracted feature vector (types and ranges) before predict_proba. Return 400 or 413 on invalid input. Add rate limiting. Add tests for malformed and oversized uploads.

verdicts.rationale: The Flask routes /upload_cv (inference) and /ranking/<job_id> (returns candidate PII) have no authentication or authorisation decorators or checks (E5, E8). The Caddy reverse proxy only terminates TLS and does not add auth (E2). The security group exposes 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (E4). The README quick-start calls the upload endpoint with no credentials (E3). The frontend fetches /ranking without any token (E1), and the test fetches it unauthenticated with a 200 response (E7). The model is loaded via pickle (E9), and the CV volume is unencrypted (E4), which adds to the exposure. The deterministic pattern check found no auth constructs.
gaps: No authentication on /upload_cv inference route
No authentication or authorisation on /ranking/<job_id>, which exposes candidate PII
No role-based authorisation for recruiters or admins
Reverse proxy adds no auth (no basic auth, forward_auth or mTLS)
Security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 with no network restriction
No rate limiting or input validation on file uploads (filename and job_id are used in paths)
Model loaded through unsafe pickle with no integrity check
No negative auth tests
verdicts.remediation: Add authentication to all routes in app/main.py, for example JWT/OAuth2 via Flask-JWT-Extended or an OIDC provider, with a decorator such as @require_role("recruiter") on /upload_cv and /ranking. Use separate admin roles for any model-management or retraining functions. Have the frontend send bearer tokens. Add proxy-level protection in Caddy (forward_auth or basic_auth) and restrict the security group CIDRs. Add rate limiting. Sanitise filename and job_id with secure_filename and validation to prevent path traversal. Verify model artefact integrity (signed hash) and move away from pickle. Add tests that expect 401/403 for unauthenticated and unauthorised requests.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence contains only application code (E1, E2) and no documented procedures for change management, pre-release validation, post-market monitoring or serious-incident reporting. E1 shows a "TODO: add audit logging before go-live" and commented-out prediction logging, which indicates monitoring and logging are not in place. The model path and threshold are set via environment variables with no versioning or validation process shown. Nothing in the evidence satisfies the quality management requirement.
gaps: No documented change management procedure for model/system updates
No pre-release validation or testing procedure
No post-market/production monitoring or drift detection
No serious-incident reporting procedure
Audit logging is unimplemented (TODO, commented-out logger)
No model versioning or approval process for REJECT_THRESHOLD/MODEL_PATH changes
verdicts.remediation: Add a QMS document set (e.g. docs/quality-management.md) covering: change management (model/threshold versioning, review and approval, rollback); pre-release validation (test sets, accuracy and bias metrics, sign-off criteria, CI gates); post-market monitoring (production performance and drift metrics, alert thresholds, review frequency); and serious-incident reporting (internal escalation, authority notification per Art. 73, timelines, owners). Implement audit logging in app/main.py (replace the TODO with structured, PII-minimised prediction logs) so monitoring and incident investigation are possible.

verdicts.rationale: The only test (E2) is a smoke test that checks for HTTP 200 on /ranking/42. It makes no metric assertions on held-out data, which the guidance says is not model validation. The training script (E1) computes accuracy on a random test split but only prints it. It has no threshold, no assertion and no build-failing gate, and no fixed seed. Nothing in the evidence (E5, E6) shows predefined metrics, thresholds or a pre-release quality gate. Deployment uses the pickled model with no validation step. This is a high-risk hiring use case with automatic rejection, so metric-based testing against thresholds is expected.
gaps: No predefined metrics or thresholds (AUC, recall, precision, etc.) appropriate to the intended purpose
No assertions on held-out data in tests
No quality gate in CI or the release process that fails the build below a threshold
Accuracy is only printed in training, not enforced, and the split has no fixed seed
No fairness or subgroup metrics for the hiring context
No documented test and validation procedure
The model artifact is not validated before deployment
verdicts.remediation: Define the acceptance metrics and thresholds in a versioned file such as config/model_acceptance.yaml. These should include AUC, precision/recall at the reject threshold, and per-group fairness metrics. Add tests/test_model_quality.py that loads the model and a fixed held-out dataset, then asserts each metric meets its threshold (for example assert auc >= 0.80). Change training/train.py to use a seeded split and to exit non-zero when thresholds are missed. Run these tests in CI as a required release gate that blocks deployment. Document the test and validation procedure and keep the results as release records. Keep the HTTP smoke test as a supplement only.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence has no privacy notice, record of processing, DPIA or any statement of an Art. 6(1) lawful basis. E1 says compliance is deferred ("later") and legal only says "probably fine". E4's "Fully GDPR compliant" claim is explicitly not evidence. The code (E5, E7) accepts CVs, scores them, auto-rejects applicants, emails them (E2) and keeps CVs forever for retraining (E6, E8). It does this with no consent capture or recording and no documented purposes or bases. Retraining on historical hiring data is a separate purpose that also has no documented basis.
gaps: No documented lawful basis per processing purpose (screening, automated rejection, rejection emails, retention, model retraining)
No privacy notice or Art. 13/14 information for applicants
No record of processing activities (Art. 30) or DPIA
No consent capture or recording mechanism, nor a documented alternative basis
No legitimate interests assessment if Art. 6(1)(f) is relied on
Retraining on stored CVs and historical hiring data has no stated basis or compatibility assessment
Compliance explicitly deferred (E1); README claim is unsupported
verdicts.remediation: 1) Add docs/ropa.md (Art. 30 record) listing each purpose (CV screening, automated scoring/rejection, rejection emails, CV retention, model training) with its Art. 6(1) basis. Cover the controller/processor roles with the Berlin customer. 2) Add a privacy notice for applicants and link it at the upload point. 3) If relying on consent, add consent capture to /upload_cv. Store the consent record (timestamp, purpose, notice version) and support withdrawal. If relying on legitimate interests or contract, add a documented LIA. 4) Complete a DPIA, since automated rejection of applicants is high risk and engages Art. 22. 5) Define a retention period instead of keep_cvs: forever, and document a separate basis for model retraining. 6) Remove the "Fully GDPR compliant" claim from the README until these are in place.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence has no privacy notice or link to one. The upload flow (E4, E7) collects CVs and personal data with no notice. The only applicant communication is a rejection email (E1) that has no controller details, purposes, legal basis, retention or rights. The README claims "Fully GDPR compliant" (E2), but E6 says compliance is deferred. E3 shows CVs are kept "forever", which is an undisclosed retention period. No privacy file exists in the excerpts.
gaps: No privacy notice file or page
No controller identity or contact details, and no DPO details
No purposes or lawful basis stated
No recipients or third-country transfer information
Retention period undisclosed (CVs kept forever)
No data subject rights or right to complain to a supervisory authority
No disclosure of automated decision-making or profiling (auto-reject) or its logic
Notice is not shown or linked at CV upload or in the rejection email
verdicts.remediation:
Add a PRIVACY.md and a hosted privacy notice covering Art. 13(1) and 13(2):
- controller and DPO contacts
- purposes and lawful basis
- recipients and transfers
- a defined retention period, replacing "keep_cvs: forever"
- the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability
- the right to complain to a supervisory authority
- the Art. 22 automated decision-making and profiling logic

Show or link the notice at CV upload (the /upload_cv flow, or the customer's application form) and in app/emailer.py's TEMPLATE. Remove the unsubstantiated "Fully GDPR compliant" claim from the README until the notice is in place.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence shows no proportionate retention period and no automated deletion. E6 sets `keep_cvs: forever` for retraining, which is the "forever" case the guidance calls non_compliant. E1 and E2 write original CVs to disk "for retraining" with no TTL or purge. The CANDIDATES dict holds PII in memory with no expiry. E5 (docker-compose) and E9 (Terraform EBS volume) define no lifecycle or purge rules. E9 also leaves the CV volume unencrypted. E7 claims "Fully GDPR compliant", but nothing supports that claim.
gaps: No retention period defined per data category (CVs, candidate profiles, scores, rejection emails)
No automated enforcement (TTL, purge job, lifecycle rule)
CVs explicitly kept forever (keep_cvs: forever)
Rejected candidates' CVs retained indefinitely for retraining with no justification or anonymisation
In-memory CANDIDATES store has no expiry
No retention period or criteria communicated to candidates (Art. 13(2)(a))
verdicts.remediation: Define a retention schedule, for example deleting rejected candidates' CVs and profiles after 6 months or less, and deleting the CVs of hired candidates once the recruitment purpose ends. Put the periods in config/settings.yaml (e.g. `cv_retention_days: 180`) and replace `keep_cvs: forever`. Add a scheduled purge job (cron or a Kubernetes CronJob) in app/ that deletes expired files under CV_DIR and expired entries in the candidate store. Replace the in-memory CANDIDATES dict with a database that has a TTL. Use only anonymised or aggregated data for retraining. Add an S3 or EBS lifecycle policy in Terraform if CVs are archived. Document the retention periods in a privacy notice and the README, and remove the unsupported "Fully GDPR compliant" claim.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence shows no deletion path for a single data subject. app/main.py (E1, E5) only exposes /upload_cv and /ranking/<job_id>, with no erase or delete endpoint. Candidate data is held in the in-memory CANDIDATES dict, and original CVs are written to disk and never removed (E1, E5). config/settings.yaml sets keep_cvs to "forever" (E4), so there is no expiry either. The CV volume is mounted at /data/cvs and is unencrypted (E3, E7), with no deletion job. Derived data is also not covered: the training data and model (E6) contain historical hiring data, and nothing shows how a subject's data would be removed from them. No documented erasure procedure appears in the excerpts. The deterministic pattern for an erase/delete function was not found.
gaps: No endpoint, admin job or script to erase a single data subject's data
Stored CV files under /data/cvs are never deleted; retention is 'forever'
No removal from the in-memory CANDIDATES store on request
No handling of derived data (training dataset, retraining copies, scores, logs, backups)
No documented erasure procedure or request-handling SLA
verdicts.remediation: Add an authenticated erasure endpoint or admin CLI, for example DELETE /candidates/<email> in app/main.py. It should (1) remove the entry from CANDIDATES or the persistent DB, (2) delete the subject's CV files under CV_DIR/<job_id>/, (3) purge the subject from the training datasets and retraining copies and exclude them from future training runs, and (4) cover backups and logs. Also add a retention limit in config/settings.yaml in place of keep_cvs: forever. Keep an audit record of each erasure that holds no personal data beyond what is needed. Write the procedure up in docs (for example docs/erasure.md), including how fast requests are handled (one month at most under GDPR Art. 12(3)), and add tests.

verdicts.rationale: The system automatically rejects applicants below a score threshold and sends rejection emails without any human review (E2, E4, E3). The code sets `override_allowed = False` and states that recruiters cannot change AI outcomes, which contradicts the README claim that recruiters can always override (E4, E2). Rejection is a legally or similarly significant decision in hiring, and the dev notes show no compliance work and only a "probably fine" legal view (E1). No contest or appeal path and no human intervention exist in the evidence.
gaps: Rejections are fully automated with no human review before they take effect
Recruiter override is disabled (override_allowed = False)
No mechanism for applicants to contest the decision or express their view
Rejection email gives no information about human review or appeal
No audit logging of decisions (TODO)
No documented Art. 22(2) exception or legal basis
README claims of override and GDPR compliance are inaccurate
verdicts.remediation: Remove the automatic rejection. Make low scores a recommendation only, and require a recruiter to review and confirm every rejection before any email is sent. Enable and implement the recruiter override and test it. import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

SENDER = "jobs@quickhire.example"

TEMPLATE = """Dear applicant,

Thank you for your interest in this position. After careful consideration we have decided not to
move forward with your application.

Kind regards,
The Hiring Team
"""


def send_rejection_email(to, job_id):
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"], msg["To"] = SENDER, to
    msg["Subject"] = f"Your application (job {job_id})"
    msg.set_content(TEMPLATE)
    with smtplib.SMTP("smtp.quickhire.example", 25) as s:
        s.send_message(msg)

services:
  api:
    build: ..
    environment:
      MODEL_PATH: /models/qh-xgb.pkl
      CV_DIR: /data/cvs
      REJECT_THRESHOLD: "0.4"
    expose: ["8080"]
    volumes:
      - /data/cvs:/data/cvs
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2.8
    ports: ["443:443"]
    command: caddy reverse-proxy --from quickhire.example --to api:8080
